speaker: Doctor
text:
Since I am inspecting a newborn presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin, I need to know if your baby was born prematurely or if there was any jaundice present within the first 24 hours of life. 

REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin_Level; REQUEST TEST: Direct_Bilirubin_Level.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That total bilirubin level of 16.1 mg/dL is significant, but since the direct bilirubin is low, this appears to be unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Was the baby feeding well immediately after birth, and has there been any dark urine or pale stools?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the mother been taking any medications, and is there any history of blood type incompatibility between you and your baby? Also, please confirm if the baby has had more than 6 wet diapers per day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (also known as Suboptimal Intake Jaundice). The combination of a total bilirubin of 16.1 mg/dL, exclusive breastfeeding, and the history of a sibling requiring liver surgery strongly suggests this diagnosis. We need to ensure adequate caloric intake to resolve this, as the low direct bilirubin rules out cholestasis or biliary atresia.
